name: Alderfern
address: Alderfern, Clone Road, Ferns, Co. Wexford
bedsNote: All three bedrooms are on the ground floor; two have en suites
tagline: A 2021 A2-rated single-storey house on half an acre at the edge of Ferns village, a short walk from two primary schools and the shop.

pros.text: Every bedroom on the ground floor
pros.detail: Single storey: bedroom 3 (3.61 × 5.23 m, en suite) suits Gabor's parents; the main bedroom also has an en suite, plus a family shower room.
BER A2 at 39.91 kWh/m²/yr with air-to-water heating and uPVC double glazing; no retrofit bill.
Stamp duty about €4,750; but €3,770/m² is high for the size.
St Edan's NS (co-ed, 39 pupils) is on Clone Road; Naomh Maodhog NS (285 pupils) is about 630 m.
Ferns Centra (7 a.m.–9 p.m.) and The Courtyard pub-restaurant are about 600–700 m away; bus stop about 490 m.
The listing describes ample space around the house and a partly elevated rear garden with countryside views (setting judged from listing text/photos).

pros.text: Cheap to run as a let
pros.detail: A2 running costs and en suites suit renting while the family is away; Courtown and the Wexford coast are within about 30 minutes.

cons.detail: Above the 100 m² floor but snug for a family of four plus summering parents; three bedrooms. A 30 m² extension would be a rough €70–100k if needed.
0.49 acres (0.2 ha), half the 1-acre target for two vizslas; fencing not mentioned.

cons.text: Dublin train is a drive and about 2 hours
cons.detail: Enniscorthy station about 13 km by road; 5 Dublin trains each weekday, about 1h50–2h20 to Connolly.
Wexford General (all ages, per HSE) is about 28 km as the crow flies, roughly 33 km by road.
Nearest mixed is Enniscorthy Community College (DEIS, ~11 km); St Mary's CBS (boys) is beside it; Coláiste Bríde is girls-only.
The listing doesn't say whether it is on mains or a well and treatment system; ask before viewing.
A 2021 build with a vaulted open-plan room, not a period or character house.
BuyerIQ's paywalled report flags one critical finding (fix cost €800–2,000, possibly radon) and an active build within 1 km; a 2021 rural build may also carry an occupancy condition.

questions: Is the house on mains water and sewer, or a private well and treatment system? If private, is there a certificate and water test?
Does the 2021 planning permission carry an occupancy or local-needs condition that would bind a buyer?
Can you send a site map of the 0.49 acres, and is the boundary fenced? Is any adjoining land for sale?
Has the house been tested for radon, and has the site or Clone Road ever flooded?
What is the active build within 1 km, and is anything planned for the fields around the house?

ai.why: A2 single-storey on the edge of Ferns, every bedroom downstairs, under budget and walkable to school and shop. Compact at 126 m² on under half an acre, and Dublin is about 2 hours by train.

electricity.detail: Connected; heat pump and 2021 build imply it, not stated.

water.detail: Not stated; mains is possible at the village edge, otherwise a well.

sewer.detail: Not stated; ask whether it is on the Ferns scheme or a treatment system.

internet.detail: Fibre likely; not in the listing, but NBI announced fibre for the townlands around Ferns (Sept 2024) and the village has open eir. BuyerIQ shows no data.

groundFloorBedroom.detail: Single storey: all three bedrooms are on the ground floor, and bedroom 3 (3.61 × 5.23 m) has its own en suite.
